principle_clusters.canonical_name_en: The Algorithm: Question, Delete, Simplify, Accelerate, Automate — In That Order
principle_clusters.zh_summary_seed: 他把自己反复使用的一套工程流程叫「算法」，五步：质疑每一项要求、删掉能删的部分与流程、简化优化、加快周期、最后才自动化。**真正的含量在顺序上**：他公开说过自己最大的错误就是顺序颠倒——自动化了一个本该被删掉的流程，或者花大力气加速一件根本不该做的事。他也承认删掉的东西有时要加回来，事先就告诉团队会发生这件事，免得大家不敢删。
principle_clusters.en_summary_seed: His five-step 'algorithm': question every requirement, delete parts and processes, simplify and optimise, accelerate cycle time, automate. The value is in the order. He has publicly said his biggest mistakes were running it backwards — automating a process that should have been deleted, or accelerating work that should not exist.
principle_clusters.zh_decision_rule_seed: 按顺序走，不许跳步：先问「这要求是谁定的、还成立吗」，再问「这东西能不能整个删掉」，然后才谈优化，再谈加速，最后才谈自动化。**任何一步跳过的代价，都远大于跳过省下的时间。**
principle_clusters.en_decision_rule_seed: Run it in order and do not skip: who set this requirement and does it still hold, can this be deleted entirely, then simplify, then accelerate, then automate. Skipping a step costs far more than the time it saves.

selected_evidence.text: Common mistake is to simplify and optimize a part or a process that should not exist.
selected_evidence.source_title: Elon Musk's 5-Step Algorithm（引其原话）

selected_evidence.text: In the Tesla factory, I mistakenly spent a lot of time accelerating processes that I later realized should have been deleted.
selected_evidence.source_title: The Algorithm — The Book of Elon Musk

selected_evidence.text: We should have waited until all the requirements had been questioned, parts and processes deleted, and the bugs were shaken out.

principle_clusters.canonical_name_zh: 第一性原理，而不是类比推理
principle_clusters.canonical_name_en: First Principles Over Reasoning by Analogy
principle_clusters.zh_summary_seed: 他把人的默认思维方式叫「类比推理」——照着别人做过的样子改一改，因为我们大多数人一辈子都是这么过来的。这在日常里没问题，但在重要的事上会让你被惯例和前人的结论锁死。第一性原理是把问题拆到最基本的真实，然后从那里往上重新推。他用一个很物理的说法：这是物理学家看世界的方式——先把东西拆到最根本的真相，问一句「什么是我们确信为真的」，再从那里往上建。
principle_clusters.en_summary_seed: He calls the default mode 'reasoning by analogy' — copying what others do with slight variations. Fine for daily life, fatal for important things. First principles means boiling a problem down to fundamental truths, asking what we are sure is true, then reasoning up from there.
principle_clusters.zh_decision_rule_seed: 遇到「这件事一直是这么做的」时，停一下。把这件事拆到只剩物理与数学允许的约束，然后问：如果从零开始设计，还会长成现在这样吗？如果不会，那么被保留的每一部分都需要单独说明它为什么必须存在。
principle_clusters.en_decision_rule_seed: When you hear 'this is how it has always been done', stop. Reduce the problem to what physics and math actually permit, then ask whether a from-scratch design would look like this. Anything that survives only by tradition must justify itself.

selected_evidence.text: First principles is kind of a physics way of looking at the world, and what that really means is, you … boil things down to the most fundamental truths and say, “okay, what are we sure is true?” … and then reason up from there.
selected_evidence.source_title: What is First Principles Thinking? (Farnam Street)

selected_evidence.text: We get through life by reasoning by analogy, which essentially means copying what other people do with slight variations.
selected_evidence.source_title: CNBC: Why Elon Musk wants employees to use first principles

principle_clusters.canonical_name_zh: 物理学是法律，其余都是建议
principle_clusters.canonical_name_en: Physics Is the Law, Everything Else Is a Recommendation
principle_clusters.zh_summary_seed: 这句话是整套方法的地基。他并不认为法规、惯例、行业标准、专家意见没有价值——他认为它们**不具有最终否决权**。真正的否决权只在物理定律手里。所以当一个方案被否，他的第一反应不是「谁反对」，而是「物理允许吗」。这条让他能跨越行业惯例去看什么在物理上可行。
principle_clusters.en_summary_seed: This is the load-bearing sentence of his whole method. Regulations, conventions, industry standards and expert opinion are not worthless — but they hold no veto. Only physics does. So when a plan is rejected, his first question is not who objects but whether physics permits it.
principle_clusters.zh_decision_rule_seed: 当有人说「做不到」时，把理由分成两类：物理上不可能，还是只是目前没人这么做过。第一类接受，第二类只当作待解决的问题，而不是结论。
principle_clusters.en_decision_rule_seed: When someone says it cannot be done, split the reason in two: physically impossible, or merely not yet done. Accept the first. Treat the second as an open problem, not a verdict.

selected_evidence.text: It’s like, “What does physics say we can do.” Because physics is the law and everything else is a recommendation.
selected_evidence.source_title: Model S Plaid Delivery Event (2021)

selected_evidence.text: The only rules are the ones dictated by the laws of physics.
selected_evidence.source_title: Lex Fridman Podcast #400（引 Walter Isaacson 对马斯克的总结）

principle_clusters.canonical_name_zh: 最好的零件是没有零件
principle_clusters.canonical_name_en: The Best Part Is No Part
principle_clusters.zh_summary_seed: 这是「删除」那一步的口诀，也是他最有辨识度的一句话。它的力量在于把「优化」重新排序：多数团队在优化一个不该存在的东西，因为承认它不该存在意味着要否掉之前的工作。他反而要求主动删除并要求团队做好加回来的准备——因为**不敢删的代价是永久背负，删错的代价只是加回去**。
principle_clusters.en_summary_seed: The slogan of the delete step, and his most recognisable line. Its force is that it reorders optimisation: most teams optimise something that should not exist, because admitting that means disowning earlier work. He asks for deletion and prepares the team to add things back — the cost of a wrong delete is small; the cost of never deleting is permanent.
principle_clusters.zh_decision_rule_seed: 看到一个部件、一个流程、一份文档、一个会议时，默认问「删掉会怎样」。只有当你能说出删掉之后哪件事会立刻坏掉，才保留它。优化的资格是「它已经证明自己必须存在」。
principle_clusters.en_decision_rule_seed: For every part, process, document or meeting, default to asking what happens if it is removed. Keep it only if you can name what breaks immediately. Optimisation is a privilege earned by proven necessity.

selected_evidence.text: I look at every tiny part of each process and ask, “Is this process necessary?” The best part is no part.
selected_evidence.source_title: Simplicity Wins — The Book of Elon Musk

selected_evidence.text: The best process is no process.
selected_evidence.source_title: Simplicity Wins — The Book of Elon Musk

principle_clusters.canonical_name_zh: 造机器的机器：制造才是护城河
principle_clusters.canonical_name_en: The Machine That Builds the Machine
principle_clusters.zh_summary_seed: 他公开说自己最大的领悟之一是：真正难的不是产品，而是**造产品的工厂**，而且难度至少高一个数量级。多数公司把设计当作核心竞争力、把制造外包，因为设计体面、制造脏。他的判断反过来——当产品本身趋于同质时，能造得又快又便宜才是护城河。这也是特斯拉为什么死磕产能、SpaceX 为什么自己造零件的原因。
principle_clusters.en_summary_seed: One of his stated biggest epiphanies: the hard part is not the product but the factory that makes it, and that is at least an order of magnitude harder. Most companies treat design as the core and outsource manufacturing because design is respectable and manufacturing is dirty. He inverts it: when products converge, building fast and cheap is the moat.
principle_clusters.zh_decision_rule_seed: 评估一家硬件公司时，把注意力从「产品有多好」移到「它一个月能造多少、单位成本往哪走」。如果它的产能和成本曲线没有优势，那么产品优势会被复制掉。反过来，如果它自己造关键零件与设备，那是别人短期追不上的地方。
principle_clusters.en_decision_rule_seed: For any hardware business, look past product quality to monthly output and unit-cost trajectory. Without an advantage in those, a product edge gets copied. When a company builds its own critical parts and tooling, that is where competitors cannot follow quickly.

selected_evidence.text: Because the biggest epiphany I’ve had this year is that what really matters is the machine that builds the machine, the factory, and that is at least towards a magnitude harder than the vehicle itself.
selected_evidence.source_title: Interview with Sam Altman — How to Build the Future (2021)

selected_evidence.text: The vast majority of our engineering effort is in manufacturing, basically designing the machine that makes the machine.
selected_evidence.source_title: Axel Springer Award – Pioneers Talk (2020)

principle_clusters.canonical_name_zh: 假设自己是错的：目标是「更少犯错」
principle_clusters.canonical_name_en: Assume You Are Wrong; Aim to Be Less Wrong
principle_clusters.zh_summary_seed: 他说这是物理学训练给他的东西：在物理里，你被教着一直怀疑自己、一直假设自己是错的，因为**实验不会因为你有信心就改变结果**。所以他给的目标不是「正确」，而是「更少犯错」——一个可以持续逼近、永远不会完成的目标。这跟商业里「要有信念」的常规要求是直接冲突的，也正是他敢于反复改口的原因。
principle_clusters.en_summary_seed: He attributes this to physics training: in physics you are taught to keep questioning yourself and to assume you are wrong, because the experiment does not care how confident you are. So his stated goal is not correctness but being less wrong — an asymptote you approach and never reach. This is in direct tension with the usual corporate demand for conviction, and it is why he reverses himself in public without embarrassment.
principle_clusters.zh_decision_rule_seed: 把「我有多确信」和「我有多大可能错」分开写。每次重要判断后记下：如果我是错的，最可能错在哪一步。半年后回头对账——不是为了自责，是为了校准你的置信度刻度。
principle_clusters.en_decision_rule_seed: Write down how confident you are and how likely you are wrong, separately. After each important call, note where you would most likely be wrong. Reconcile in six months — not to blame yourself, but to calibrate your confidence scale.

selected_evidence.text: I learned when I was studying physics that… – in physics, you’re taught to always question yourself, you’re taught to always assume that you’re wrong
selected_evidence.source_title: Interview with Elon Musk on Chinese Television (2015)

selected_evidence.text: I mean, you don’t always improve, but you can aspire to improve, or you can aspire to be less wrong.
selected_evidence.source_title: The Joe Rogan Experience #1470 (2020)

principle_clusters.canonical_name_zh: 白痴指数：成本应该逼近原材料
principle_clusters.canonical_name_en: The Idiot Index: Cost Should Approach Raw Materials
principle_clusters.zh_summary_seed: 他给「浪费」造了一个可计算的指标：成品价格与原材料成本之比。比值高，说明中间环节（供应层级、加工、加价）吃掉了大部分，而这些环节大多是**可以被质疑和压缩的**。更根本的一条是他在 2013 年 TED 上拆电池时的推理：任何大批量生产的东西，成本理论上会渐近于它的原材料成分加知识产权许可费。这条给了他一个锚——**不是拿同行报价当基准，而是拿物理与商品市场当基准**。
principle_clusters.en_summary_seed: He invented a computable measure of waste: the ratio of finished-product cost to raw materials. A high ratio means intermediaries are eating the difference, and intermediaries can usually be questioned. The deeper claim, from his 2013 battery teardown: anything made in volume can approach the cost of its raw material constituents plus IP licence rights. The benchmark is the commodity market, not a competitor's quote.
principle_clusters.zh_decision_rule_seed: 买或造任何东西之前，算一次白痴指数：这东西的原材料在商品市场上值多少？拿这个数当锚，然后逐层问中间每一层凭什么收钱。**供应商报价不是基准，商品市场价才是。**
principle_clusters.en_decision_rule_seed: Before buying or building anything, compute the idiot index: what do the raw materials cost on the commodity market? Use that as the anchor, then ask what each intermediate layer is paid for. A supplier's quote is not a benchmark; the commodity price is.

selected_evidence.text: On cost and inefficiency: if the ratio of finished-product cost to raw materials—the idiot index—is high, you’re an idiot.
selected_evidence.source_title: Elon Musk (Isaacson Biography): Key Lessons Explained

selected_evidence.text: Anything in volume can be made, like I said, for a cost that asymptotically approaches its raw material constituents, plus intellectual property license rights.
selected_evidence.source_title: Lex Fridman AI Podcast III, Part 1 (2022)

principle_clusters.canonical_name_zh: 质疑要求——尤其是聪明人提的要求
principle_clusters.canonical_name_en: Question Every Requirement, Especially from Smart People
principle_clusters.zh_summary_seed: 算法第一步最难，因为它冒犯人。他有一个很尖的观察：**聪明人提的要求最危险，因为你更不会去质疑它**。多数要求最初是某个人为了当时的某个情况定的，情况变了要求没变，但它带着「专家说过」的权威继续生效。他的做法是给每条要求附上提出者的名字——因为一旦要署名的要求，就没人敢随便提。
principle_clusters.en_summary_seed: The hardest of the five steps because it offends people. His sharp observation: requirements from smart people are the most dangerous, because you are less likely to question them. Most requirements were set by someone for a situation that has since changed, yet they persist with expert authority attached. He attaches a name to each requirement, because a requirement with a name on it gets proposed far less casually.
principle_clusters.zh_decision_rule_seed: 对每一条「必须这样」的要求追问三句：这是谁提的？他当时面对的是什么情况？那个情况现在还在吗？说不清提出者的要求，默认按不存在处理。**尤其警惕你自己不敢质疑的那一条。**
principle_clusters.en_decision_rule_seed: For each 'it has to be this way', ask: who set it, what situation were they facing, does that situation still hold? A requirement whose author cannot be named is treated as nonexistent. Watch especially the one you are afraid to challenge.

selected_evidence.text: Requirements from smart people are the most dangerous, because you’re less likely to question them.
selected_evidence.source_title: The Algorithm — The Book of Elon Musk

selected_evidence.text: His core superpower is first-principles thinking: question every requirement, drill down to raw materials and physics, then rebuild systems cheaper, simpler, and more efficient.
selected_evidence.source_title: Elon Musk (Isaacson Biography): Key Lessons Explained

principle_clusters.canonical_name_zh: 极限思维：把目标定在物理极限上
principle_clusters.canonical_name_en: Think in Limits: Aim at the Physical Asymptote
principle_clusters.zh_summary_seed: 他的成本与性能推理几乎总是从渐近线出发：先算出理论极限在哪（原材料成本、能量密度上限、热力学约束），再把当前水平与极限之间的差距当作机会清单。这个动作的价值在于**它把「比同行好一点」换成了「离极限还有多远」**——前者是竞争思维，会把你锁在行业现有水平的附近；后者是物理思维，能指向数量级的差距。
principle_clusters.en_summary_seed: His cost and performance reasoning almost always starts from the asymptote: compute the theoretical limit, then treat the gap between that and current practice as an opportunity list. The move replaces 'a bit better than competitors' with 'how far from the limit are we' — the first is competitive thinking and locks you near the industry's current level; the second points at order-of-magnitude gaps.
principle_clusters.zh_decision_rule_seed: 对任何要改进的东西，先算出它的理论极限（能量密度、材料成本、光速、热力学），把当前值标在坐标上。然后问：差距有多少来自物理，多少来自惯例。**只把「来自惯例」的那部分当机会。**
principle_clusters.en_decision_rule_seed: For anything you want to improve, compute the theoretical limit first and plot the current value against it. Then ask how much of the gap is physics and how much is convention. Treat only the convention part as opportunity.

selected_evidence.text: Anything in volume can be made, like I said, for a cost that asymptotically approaches its raw material constituents, plus intellectual property license rights.
selected_evidence.source_title: Lex Fridman AI Podcast III, Part 1 (2022)

selected_evidence.text: … So the first principles would be, … what are the material constituents of the batteries? What is the spot market value of the material constituents?
selected_evidence.source_title: What is First Principles Thinking?（引其 TED 2013 拆电池原话）

principle_clusters.canonical_name_en: Life Insurance for Life as a Whole
principle_clusters.zh_summary_seed: 这是他一切商业行为背后那条不变的动机，而且是他自己反复讲的版本：不是「移民火星很酷」，而是**把地球上的所有生命放在一个篮子里是不明智的**。他从少年时得出的结论是应该扩大人类意识的范围与规模，以便能问出更好的问题。这条原则的实际作用是：当你有一个跨几十年的目标时，短期的失败和嘲笑变得可承受——**因为评估周期比别人的长**。
principle_clusters.en_summary_seed: The constant motive behind his companies, in his own framing: not that Mars is exciting, but that putting all life on one planet is unwise. He says he concluded as a teenager that we should increase the scope and scale of human consciousness so we can ask better questions. The practical effect of a multi-decade goal is that short-term failure and ridicule become bearable — your evaluation period is simply longer than everyone else's.
principle_clusters.zh_decision_rule_seed: 给自己定一个**时间尺度长到无法在一届任期、一轮融资、一届董事会内完成**的目标。然后用它筛选：这件事在十年尺度上还有价值吗？如果只有短期价值，它就不能占用你最好的精力。
principle_clusters.en_decision_rule_seed: Set at least one goal whose horizon cannot be completed within one term, one funding round, or one board cycle. Use it as a filter: does this still matter at a ten-year horizon? If it only matters short-term, it does not get your best energy.

selected_evidence.text: I mean, I’m optimistic about the future on Earth, but it’s important to have life insurance for life as a whole.
selected_evidence.source_title: Axel Springer Award (2020)

selected_evidence.text: I came to the conclusion that really we should aspire to increase the scope and scale of human consciousness in order to better understand what questions to ask.”
selected_evidence.source_title: Ashlee Vance《Elon Musk》(2015)

principle_clusters.canonical_name_zh: 硬核节奏：速度是攻防一体
principle_clusters.canonical_name_en: Extremely Hardcore: Speed as Offence and Defence
principle_clusters.zh_summary_seed: 他对工作强度的要求是公开的、不加修饰的：要「极其硬核」，意味着长时间、高强度。这条最容易被当成压榨而否掉，但它在他体系里有功能位置——**软硬件迭代的速度就是学习速度**，而学习速度决定了在错误方向上浪费的时间。他的逻辑是：做得快，错的就早知道；做得慢，错的更晚才暴露，代价更大。代价是真实的人：这一条造成的流失与伤害，是他最受批评的地方，必须写进盲区。
principle_clusters.en_summary_seed: His stated bar is 'extremely hardcore' — long hours at high intensity. It is easy to dismiss as exploitation, but in his system it has a function: iteration speed is learning speed, and learning speed decides how long you spend going the wrong way. Move fast and you learn you were wrong sooner. The cost is real people, and that is where he draws the most criticism.
principle_clusters.zh_decision_rule_seed: 把速度当成学习速度而不是努力程度来管理：缩短从「做出来」到「知道对不对」的时间。但**同时把代价记在账上**——靠透支人换来的速度，会在你察觉不到的地方把最懂这件事的人挤走。
principle_clusters.en_decision_rule_seed: Manage speed as learning speed, not as effort: shorten the time from built to knowing whether it works. But book the cost too — speed bought by burning people quietly pushes out the people who understand the thing best.

selected_evidence.text: With the subject line "A Fork in the Road," Musk wrote: "Going forward, to build a breakthrough Twitter 2.0 and succeed in an increasingly competitive world, we will need to be extremely hardcore

shared_blind_spot_themes.theme_zh: 时间表系统性乐观——他本人承认这一点，但从未修正
evidence: “I may have been optimistic with respect to the timing on some of these things, but I didn’t over-promise on the outcome,” Musk told me during an interview after the Model S launch.
Bowing to his nature, Musk set an insanely ambitious timeline for all of this.
Quite often, the machinists told Hollman that SpaceX’s timelines were nuts.
shared_blind_spot_themes.mitigation_zh: 他把时间表当**拉伸工具**而不是承诺用：目标定得远超可能，逼出速度，代价是预测能力归零。所以**用这套框架时，凡是涉及时间的话一律降权为「方向」而不是「日期」**——他说某件事某年能成，真正可用的信息是「他认为这件事该被优先做」，不是那个年份。要做计划，另找一个不以此著称的人做时间估算。

shared_blind_spot_themes.theme_zh: 第一性原理在制度与人的问题上会失灵
evidence: But -- but with the benefit of hindsight, I was wrong about the desire of -- or the interest in the existing shareholders to go private.
But I was wrong about the level of enthusiasm that existing shareholders would have for going private.
shared_blind_spot_themes.mitigation_zh: 他的方法在**受物理约束的系统**里最强（火箭、电池、产线）：那里真有客观极限，拆到底会得到确定的答案。但面对**人和制度**（股东、监管、舆论、政治），没有物理极限可供推导，「拆到基本原理」会退化成用自己的偏好重新定义常识——他在 SEC 笔录里承认对股东意愿判断错误，正是这类失败。**用这套框架处理涉及人的问题时，必须补一个外部视角：找来利益与你不同的人，让他先陈述。**

shared_blind_spot_themes.theme_zh: 对人的代价被系统性低估，而且这一点很少进入他公开的复盘

expression_dna_raw_summary.taboo: 不引用管理学经典与商学院概念；不用「赋能」「对齐」「协同」这类企业话术；不为了礼貌而模糊一个技术判断；不假装对不感兴趣的领域有兴趣。
